objectives: Assess growth faltering with nutrition-focused history and exam.
Screen for severe malnutrition danger signs before routine counseling.
Build a practical feeding and follow-up plan for HC III caregivers.
takeaways: Very low weight needs trend interpretation and feeding assessment, not vitamins alone.
Check bilateral oedema, appetite, lethargy, and recurrent infections to identify severe risk.
Counseling should include meal frequency, feeding during illness, and scheduled re-weighing.
learnCaseOverrides.blurb: A toddler with poor growth and recurrent diarrhoea needs structured nutrition assessment and follow-up planning.

sections.title: Chief complaint
sections.text: Poor weight gain and frequent illness

sections.title: Caregiver statement
sections.text: Grandmother says child eats small amounts and has had recurrent diarrhoea episodes.

coach.title: Maria is visibly underweight
coach.body: Start with danger signs, then move to feeding quality and illness contributors.

sections.title: Severe malnutrition screen
sections.reveal_note: No oedema; appetite reduced but still taking food.

coach.title: What is the best immediate approach?
coach.body: Choose an action that avoids both neglect and over-referral.

question.prompt: What should guide your next step?

options.text: Perform full feeding assessment and growth counseling, with close weight follow-up
Give appetite stimulant only and no counseling
Ignore nutrition and treat only intermittent fever complaints
Declare severe oedematous malnutrition despite absent oedema

question.right: Correct. Growth faltering requires feeding assessment, infection review, and structured follow-up when severe danger signs are absent.
question.wrong: Quick-fix medication without feeding review misses the root problem and delays recovery.

sections.title: Feeding history reveal
sections.text: Child gets thin porridge twice daily, minimal protein foods, and feeding is reduced during illness.

sections.title: Nutrition plan
sections.detail: Energy-dense local foods, frequent meals, continued feeding during illness, deworming review as age-appropriate

coach.title: Which plan is best for this family?
coach.body: Select realistic recommendations for HC III follow-up.

question.prompt: What is the best management plan now?

options.text: Provide specific feeding plan, treat intercurrent illness, and re-weigh in 2 weeks
Delay any follow-up until three months later
Stop breastfeeding immediately to encourage solid foods

question.right: Correct. Practical food counseling with short-interval recheck is central to growth-faltering management.
question.wrong: Delaying follow-up or restricting feeding worsens undernutrition and illness vulnerability.

sections.title: Case outcome
sections.text: You identified growth faltering and created a realistic caregiver-centered nutrition plan.
sections.emphasis: Structured feeding review is the core intervention.

coach.title: Key teaching points
coach.body: Very low weight in toddlers demands careful nutrition history, danger-sign screening, and short-interval follow-up. Counseling quality strongly affects outcomes.
